entity: Acute Care Department Contact & Golden Triage Rule
content: Department Contact: Alishia Evan (Front Desk / Contact Center). Golden Rule: Never book emergency red flags directly, and never schedule urgent symptoms for hours later or late at night!

entity: STOP — Emergency Red Flags (Do NOT Book Direct)
content: Phone Callers: Do NOT put these patients on the schedule right away! Put the caller on hold (or alert staff immediately) and get a triage nurse or doctor on duty to decide if the patient should come in or go straight to the ER / call 911. Walk-In Rule: Bring walk-in patients with red flags straight to the back clinical area immediately for vitals or an EKG—never turn them away at the front counter. Red Flag Symptoms: Chest pain; shortness of breath / trouble breathing; heart fluttering / racing / palpitations (especially with chest pain, dizziness, or fainting); severe stomach / belly pain (nurse/MD must screen for location, pregnancy, fever/vomiting, black/bloody stool, or groin/pelvic pain); testicle pain or discomfort (possible twisted testicle surgical emergency); vaginal bleeding or pelvic pain in pregnant or possibly pregnant women; stroke warning signs (slurred speech, sudden severe headache, confusion, numbness/tingling, one-sided weakness, trouble walking -> ER/911 immediately); neck pain after accident/injury; head injury with loss of consciousness, severe headache, confusion, memory loss, or repeated vomiting; neck pain + severe headache + stiff neck + fever (meningitis -> ER immediately).

rules.walkin_action: Bring Straight to Back Clinical Area

entity: PAUSE — Mandatory Screening Questions (Allergic Reactions & Headaches)
content: Allergic Reaction / Rash / Swelling — Ask all 4 questions first: (1) Trouble breathing, wheezing, or throat tightness? (2) Trouble swallowing, or tongue/throat swelling? (3) Dizzy, lightheaded, or feeling like passing out? (4) Recent exposure to a known severe allergy trigger (bee sting, peanuts, shellfish, medication) or already used an EpiPen? If YES to any: Do NOT book; alert nurse/MD immediately (ER/911 for phone callers). If NO to all: Safe to book for mild rash, hives, itching, or minor swelling (if EpiPen was already used, check with nurse/MD first). Headache — Ask all 4 questions first: (1) Hit suddenly like a 'thunderclap' or 'worst headache of your life'? (2) Fever, stiff neck, or new rash? (3) Trouble seeing, talking, walking, or numbness/weakness? (4) Passed out or almost passed out? If YES to any: Do NOT book; alert nurse/MD and instruct ER/911. If NO to all: Safe to book (migraines, tension, sinus pressure, mild ongoing headaches).

entity: GO — Conditions Safe to Book Directly into Acute Care
content: Once emergency red flags are ruled out, book directly into an open Acute Care slot: ENT & Eyes: Sore throat, cough, sinus pain or stuffy nose, earache or ear swelling, pink eye / red or watery eye (ask Left or Right), mild wheezing (with no trouble breathing). Stomach, Bathroom & Women's Health: Mild or moderate stomach ache, nausea or throwing up, diarrhea (no severe dehydration or blood), constipation, pain or burning when peeing (possible UTI), vaginal discharge or yeast infection, white patches in mouth (thrush). Skin, Pain & Minor Injuries: Rash or diaper rash, bug or tick bite, skin boil or abscess, splinter or foreign body in hand/ear/nose, cuts/lacerations, hurt fingernail, stuck earring, ingrown toenail (same-day only), back/rib/muscle pain, limping, fever, fussy/crying child, tooth pain, breast infection (mastitis), mild dizziness or general tiredness (no stroke signs).

entity: Acute Care Slot Lengths, Ingrown Toenails & Non-Covered Services
content: Regular Acute Visit: 15 minutes (default slot length for normal sick visits). Cuts / Stitches (Lacerations / Suturing): 30 minutes (always ask Left vs. Right and exact body part/finger/toe so nurses can prep supply cart). Stitch / Suture Removal: 15 minutes (book into any open slot right away). Hemorrhoids: 30 minutes (for female patients, inform her while booking that the doctor is male and a female nurse will stay in the room as a chaperone). Ingrown Toenails (Procedure Slot): SAME-DAY ONLY (never book for a future date or tomorrow); Max 2 Per Day (check yellow note at top of schedule: '2 same day appt ingrowns'); Strictly 3 Doctors Only: Dr. Gildin, Dr. Lob, or Dr. Zhang (never book with part-time or per diem doctors). What Acute Care Does NOT Do: No Routine Medication Refills (refer to regular PCP in Adult Medicine or Pediatrics); No IV Fluids or IV Medicine (direct patient to Emergency Room).

entity: Dr. Dittmeier Cell Phone Rule & Left vs. Right Laterality Checklist
content: Dr. Robert Dittmeier's Cell Phone Rule: If ever unsure whether a patient should be booked on Dr. Dittmeier's schedule, call him directly on his cell phone (whether in clinic or at home)—he prefers speaking directly rather than having another doctor or nurse screen his patients (if he doesn't answer, ask nurse/MD on duty). Always Ask Left vs. Right: For cuts, bone/joint injuries, or eye issues, always clarify Left vs. Right and the exact spot (specific finger: Thumb, Index, Middle, Ring, Pinky; specific toe: Big, 2nd, Middle, 4th, Pinky; upper/lower eyelid, eyebrow, etc.) so nurses can open the right template and prep the supply cart.

entity: Bakertown Clinic On-Site Illnesses & Minor Procedures
content: Common Illnesses Treated at Bakertown: Sore throat / Strep (rapid strep swab & throat cultures); COVID-19 & Flu (rapid testing & treatment); Colds & Sinus Infections (URIs & sinusitis); Ear & Eye Infections (otitis media, swimmer's ear / otitis externa, conjunctivitis); UTIs (in-office urine dipstick + send to lab workflow); Skin Infections (cellulitis, impetigo, folliculitis). Minor Hands-On Procedures at Bakertown: Cuts & Stitches (simple/intermediate laceration repair, 30 min); Boil / Abscess Drainage (I&D); Ingrown Toenail Removal (same-day only, max 2/day with Dr. Gildin, Dr. Lob, or Dr. Zhang); Splinter & Surface Foreign Body Removal; Earwax Removal (cerumen removal); Wound Care & Dressing Changes; Stitch & Staple Removal (15 min).
